title: serve s3: uses too much memory on multipart uploads
body:
When uploading multipart files `serve s3` holds all the parts in memory. This is a documented limitaton of the library rclone uses for serving S3.

comments.author: participant2
reporter
comments.body:
> Seems to me that's an issue with the gofakes3 lib rclone is using.

Yes it is.

> The body of a part is stored in memory.
> 
> The suggestions that I can make is as rclone serve s3 is considering the root path as root of all buckets :
> 
> * Either we use local cache file to implement `mpu.parts[partNumber]` ,

This could be done very easily using `--vfs-cache-mode writes` - this would assemble the file on disk then upload it when it was finished. This has the disadvantage that you need local disk space and that the file doesn't get uploaded until the end. It would work with all backends though.

> * Either we use /uploads/bucket-name/multipart-upload-{id}/part_{id}.

We have the problem then that we need to join the chunks back together when they are downloaded. This isn't impossible but it is quite a bit of extra work.

A third option would be for backends which support [OpenChunkWriter](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/4e07a72dc7f9cdd2b458f5c0f382f00147a0bd9b/fs/features.go#L176) or [OpenWriterAt](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/4e07a72dc7f9cdd2b458f5c0f382f00147a0bd9b/fs/features.go#L169) to send the chunks directly to the backend. This was my original plan and would work very well with backends which support that, but not at all with other backends.

> This could be done with an option to provide an existing path to VFS.
> 
> BTW would be wise to integrate gofakes3 lib into rclone repo as it is not widely used / reviewed and could be an target of choice for a malicious actor.

@participant5 we discussed transferring the gofakes3 fork to the rclone organisation - would you still like to do that? If so let me know and I'll send you instructions.

> Missed sth : I can provide with a PR if this approach is ok for you.

Offer of a PR is great! I think we need to sort out the right approach and where gofakes3 is living first but yes - thank you.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have made a stab at making this work. The chunks are sent straight to the backend and aren't buffered in memory or on disk. Only the chunks being received are buffered in memory until they have been written to the backend.

[v1.75.0-beta.9734.52dd8ad4a.fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart](https://<redacted-host>/branch/fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart/v1.75.0-beta.9734.52dd8ad4a.fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart/) on branch [fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/tree/fix-7453-s3-serve-multipart) (uploaded in 15-30 mins)

Testing appreciated :-)

Note that it only supports backends which support OpenChunkWriter or OpenWriterAt. This includes s3, b2, azureblob, oracleobjectstorage, drime, filen, archive, sftp, local and azurefiles I think.

For all other backends it will fall back to buffering in memory like it does at the moment.

You can also try --use-mmap which will cause memory to be released immediately.

You can also use --max-buffer-memory to cap the total memory use

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
the multipart upload is failing right out the gate like this:

```
rclone-s3-proxy 2026/06/08 09:23:03 ERROR : serve s3: failed to upload chunk 1 with 21501088 bytes: operation error S3: UploadPart, serialization failed: crypt: partEncrypter unsupported seek
rclone-s3-proxy 2026/06/08 09:23:04 ERROR : serve s3: crypt: overlapping multipart parts - all parts except the last must be the same size
rclone-s3-proxy 2026/06/08 09:23:04 ERROR : serve s3: crypt: overlapping multipart parts - all parts except the last must be the same size
rclone-s3-proxy 2026/06/08 09:23:06 ERROR : serve s3: crypt: overlapping multipart parts - all parts except the last must be the same size
rclone-s3-proxy 2026/06/08 09:23:14 ERROR : serve s3: crypt: overlapping multipart parts - all parts except the last must be the same size
```

command i run rclone with:

`rclone serve s3 --addr $(SERVES3_ENDPOINT) --vfs-fast-fingerprint --auth-key $(RCLONE_S3PROXY_ACCESS_KEY_ID),$(RCLONE_S3PROXY_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY) $(SERVES3_BACKEND):`

rclone config (sans access keys, of course):

```
  RCLONE_CONFIG_CRYPTED_REMOTE: s3remote:test-bucket
  RCLONE_CONFIG_CRYPTED_TYPE: crypt
  RCLONE_CONFIG_S3REMOTE_ENDPOINT: https://rgw.test.xyz
  RCLONE_CONFIG_S3REMOTE_PROVIDER: Ceph
  RCLONE_CONFIG_S3REMOTE_TYPE: s3
  RCLONE_CRYPT_DIRECTORY_NAME_ENCRYPTION: "false"
  RCLONE_CRYPT_FILENAME_ENCRYPTION: "off"
  S3REMOTE_BUCKET: test-bucket
  SERVES3_BACKEND: crypted
  SERVES3_ENDPOINT: 0.0.0.0:8088
  SERVES3_VIRTUAL_BUCKET: encrypted-backups
```

At  the same time, the archiving of WAL files seems to work just fine, as it is writing the single WAL files to the objectstore. These are only mebibytes in size, though, so not multipart.


The problem seems to be as following: PG-Barman has a size overshoot when putting data in chunks, so it seems to not be able  to create uniform chunks.

```
def write(self, buf):
    if self.buffer and self.buffer.tell() > self.chunk_size:
        self.flush()
```

The write buffer on PG-Barman flushes whenever the buffer exceeds chunk_size  (5 Mi), producing variably sized upload parts.

Is there a way to implement the fix on rclone side without having to resort to uniform chunk sizes? Evidently, many applications do not natively write in fixed size chunks.
